result.title: Can You Undo It? Reversibility Classes for AI Agent Actions
result.summary: Tool-using AI agents change files, databases, access rights and public information, yet permission to call a tool does not establish whether a mistake can be undone. We present Reversibility Classes, a declared five-level vocabulary with argument-sensitive rules, conservative defaults and an explicit prior-state capture contract. The pinned implementation and evidence-linked registry cover 536 tools across 20 MCP servers. All 738 rule-case checks conform to declared expectations, while native annotation mapping differs from draft registry labels for 118 of 481 comparable tools. One AI-assisted reviewer approves 148 ratings, 75 matching the registry; this is not independent agreement. On 2,158 recorded runs, the implemented session guard gates the associated action in all 29 attributable attack-positive runs, compared with 18 for a read/write proxy, while adding nine approval points across 1,209 benign runs. Controlled file, Git, SQLite and three-browser experiments show that recovery depends on captured state, later changes, editor storage and recovery route, and expose a Git merge-state exception. The evidence supports making recovery assumptions explicit and testable. It does not establish registry-wide accuracy, reduced production harm or general recovery reliability.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「可逆性等级」这一五级声明式词汇（含参数敏感规则、保守默认与前置状态捕获契约），覆盖20个MCP服务器、536个工具并附证据链接注册表，通过规则一致性检查、AI辅助评分、2158次记录运行的会话守护评估，以及文件、Git、SQLite与浏览器实验考察恢复是否可行。
AI.relevance_reason: 「动作是否可撤销」可作为一种行动代价信号，可能与 latent 推理中的停止/继续取证决策及前置状态捕获的表示要求相关，但该文关注 agent 安全分类而非视觉推理，联系需较多核查。
